citations.narrative:
The facility did not have an accurate record of dispositions of animals that have died at the facility since the last
inspection. Three adult chinchillas were verbally reported to have died since the last inspection on 30-September-2026;
however, these deaths were not documented on a disposition record.
A facility representative recorded the dates of death for the animals at the time of inspection.
Improper recordkeeping does not allow APHIS officials to properly account for animals on the premises or allow for proper
tracking of animals. Each dealer and exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly
disclose all information required by the AWA concerning each animal purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, or
otherwise in his or her possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, euthanized, sold, or otherwise
disposed of by that dealer or exhibitor.

The animal housing area in building one is not being adequately maintained in good repair and does not protect the
animals from injury:
In approximately 58 enclosures, there were jagged edges found in the metal feeders.
There were various sharp points on metal wiring of the enclosure fronts or doors of approximately 50 enclosures.
Jagged edges and sharp points could result in injury to the regulated animals. The facility must be constructed of such
material and of such strength as appropriate for the animals involved. The indoor and outdoor housing facilities shall be
structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to contain the animals.
Correct by ensuring that housing facilities are maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to safely
contain the animals.

The facility is not adequately cleaning the premises. In building #1, there were areas that contained excessive amounts of
cobwebs. These areas include:
-In room #1 near the front entrance there were numerous cobwebs observed above two enclosures housing
approximately two adult chinchillas.
-In room #1 in the back of the room there were numerous cobwebs observed above several enclosures housing
approximately four adult chinchillas.
-In room #2 numerous cobwebs were seen above the enclosures and on the front of the enclosures near the water lines.
-In room #3 numerous cobwebs were seen above the enclosures and on the front and back of the enclosures.
Failure to adequately clean the animal enclosures and areas near the enclosures can lead to illness, transmission of
diseases, and attract unwanted pests. The facility must ensure that the premises are kept clean and in good repair to
protect the animals from injury and to facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with Facility Representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:

Mailstop #3W11
